title: token-bucket-federation-sim-notes
body:
Purpose:
Short scratchpad for a federated token-bucket quota model across client (SDK), edge proxies, and Redwood runtime. Goal is a lightweight, failure-resilient scheme that permits local smoothing and graceful spillback while preserving global fairness and accounting.

Motivation / Background:
- Current per-tenant server-side token buckets cause sharp head-of-line drops under bursty mobile/internet conditions.
- Clients/endpoints want predictable short-term throughput even when network is flaky.
- Full central arbitration (RPC to control-plane for every request) is too heavy/latency-sensitive.

Design goals:
- Local smoothing: allow short token bursts at client/edge without blowing commit limits.
- Global correctness: long-term consumption must match server-accounted usage (no double-spend).
- Robust to partitions: clients can operate offline for short windows and reconcile later with deterministic outcomes.
- Low telemetry/ops cost: minimize heartbeat load and storage.
- Safe-by-default: fail closed for high-risk actions (e.g., request that touches PII) unless server authorizes.

High level idea (sketch):
- Each tenant has a server-side authoritative bucket: capacity C_global, refill R_global/sec.
- We hand out small time-bound "leases" to edge proxies and SDK instances: (lease_id, allowance A, expiry T_exp, epoch).
- SDK/edge maintains a local bucket (capacity A_local initially = A). Consumption consumes local tokens immediately.
- At lease expiry or before local allowance depleted, a renewal request is sent to server to top-up (or request larger lease).
- Server uses a linearized ledger (append-only events) to guarantee total tokens issued <= available over time.
- Reconciliation path: if client used more tokens than were finally allowed (e.g., used offline expired tokens), server records an overdraw event and applies soft penalties or rejects future leases. In practice we prefer conservative leases to avoid overdraw as normal mode.

Lease shape (API prototype):
- GET /v1/tenants/{tid}/leases?want=A_desired&ttl_seconds=60
  Response (200):
  {
    "lease_id": "L-<uuid>",
    "allowed_tokens": 120,
    "expiry": "2024-11-18T15:04:05Z",
    "epoch": 17,
    "reservoir_id": "R-edge-3",
    "sig": "base64sig"  // optional short HMAC to prevent tampering
  }

- POST /v1/tenants/{tid}/consume
  Body:
  {
    "lease_id": "L-...",
    "tokens": 1,
    "client_ts": "2024-11-18T15:03:32Z",
    "operation": "generate"
  }
  Server semantics: idempotent accept, records consumption against lease, returns current server-balance. For low-latency, SDK should not wait for POST success to use local token (optimistic).

Local config (SDK/edge) sketch (yaml-like):
- max_local_lease: 200  # absolute cap client will request
- min_lease_slice: 20   # prefer smaller frequent leases for fairness
- expiry_window_sec: 8  # attempt renewal this many seconds before expiry
- offline_tolerance: 30 # allow token usage up to this many seconds after lost connectivity before rejecting risky ops
- conservative_backoff: true  # low-priority tenants request smaller leases on congestion

Sequence / ASCII flow (happy path):
Client                Edge                 Server
  |----lease req----->|----forward req---->|
  |<---lease (A=60)--|<---lease resp------|
  |--consume local--->|                   |  (local decrements)
  | (when low) renew ->|----renew--------->|
  |                    |<---new lease------|
  |  send async consume postings (batched) ->|
  |                    |                    |  (server appends consumption events)

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Lost lease renewal (client still has tokens): client uses local until expiry then rate-limits. Server rejects any consume posts beyond lease expiry.
- Double-spend across multi-edge: server-issued epoch + reservoir_id prevents two reservoirs receiving more than global share. Leases tied to reservoir help debugging and throttling.
- Replay attacks: lease HMAC + nonce in consume posting; server idempotency keyed by (lease_id, seq).

Costing and telemetry:
- Server stores lightweight ledger: entries: {ts, tenant, lease_id, tokens_claimed, source}. This is append-only and is prunable by epoch window (keep rolling 90d).
- Emit aggregated metrics: lease-granted-rate, lease-deny-rate, average-lease-size by tenant tier, overdraw events.
- Edge/SDK emits small periodic heartbeat: last_seq, tokens_outstanding. Heartbeat every 30s amortized; clients with no heartbeat are downgraded to minimal leases.

Simulation notes (what I hacked locally):
- Simple discrete-event sim that models N clients per tenant, each client request process Poisson lambda.
- Variables to sweep: global refill, max_lease_size, renewal_latency, network-partition probability.
- Observed: smaller leases + faster renewal trades latency for global fairness; larger leases reduce server CPU but inflate variance and occasional overdraws.

Open questions / tradeoffs (rough):
- How to treat long-tail offline clients (days offline) vs short transient dropouts? (Probably revoke offline leases aggressively and require explicit re-auth for >hours).
- What penalty model for overdraw? Immediate reject vs soft-billing? Need product input on commercial implications.
- Should leases be signed by server HMAC only, or also tied to client id + TLS cert? Trade: security vs issuance complexity.
- Do we allow leases to be transferable (handed from edge to client)? Transfer increases complexity; prefer reservoir-scoped leases that are not transferable.
- How to handle cross-tenant bursts (multi-tenant noisy neighbor)? Should server keep burst buffer per-tenant and throttle by tier?

Next steps / TODOs:
- Share with infra/serving runtime for feedback (Ethan/Maya) -- check reservoir concept alignment with allocator.
- Formalize lease API payloads and HMAC key rotation plan.
- Run sim sweep with product-driven parameter sets (SLA tiers).
- Prototype client SDK behavior: conservative and optimistic modes.
- Draft telemetry dashboards: lease churn, renewal latency, overdraw incident count.

Notes to self:
- Keep default lease size small (20-60 tokens) for hosted free tiers; larger for dedicated.
- Consider "one-time" privileged tokens for high-sensitivity operations that require server ack.
- If implementing, gate behind feature-flag and test on a single low-traffic tenant first.

References:
- inspiration: gRPC flow-control token patterns, HTTP/2 windowing ideas, Akamai edge reservation papers (notes), prior Redwood TTL leasing experiments (internal).

End of scratchpad.
